Bullish stock is taking a hit today.
Issuer Sponsored Token Coalition and Shareholder Rights
The afternoon slide follows Thursday’s announcement that Bullish, alongside
, a shareholder-services firm Bullish is in the process of acquiring, has convened the Issuer Sponsored Token Coalition. Joined by infrastructure providers
, the working group aims to establish technical standards and regulatory frameworks for the next generation of tokenized public securities.

Crucially, the coalition is focused on an “issuer-sponsored” model. Unlike existing tokenized products that merely replicate the price movements of a stock and provide synthetic economic exposure, Bullish’s framework seeks to connect digital tokens directly to a company’s authoritative shareholder register. This infrastructure is designed to guarantee that token holders retain actual legal ownership, including voting rights, dividend distributions, and corporate-action entitlements.

The launch of the coalition directly follows a September 17 exemption issued by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission that permits limited on-chain trading of U.S.-listed equities. By spearheading this initiative, Bullish is attempting to build the foundational interoperability required to bridge traditional clearing systems with blockchain networks.

While the coalition does not immediately launch a new retail product or bind participants to commercial agreements, it signals a strategic push by Bullish to dominate the digital-asset market infrastructure layer. Coalition members are scheduled to convene with corporate issuers at the
on October 27 to further evaluate smart-contract architectures, regulatory compliance, and potential pilot programs.
Bullish shares were down 4.91% at $37.74 at the time of publication on Friday,
